blocks.heading: Packaging does work
blocks.text: Packaging is the physical container or wrapping for a product, also used for promotional purposes. It can protect contents, contain portions, preserve quality, make handling and transport easier, supply instructions or information and support recognition on display. Explain the function and consequence: a secure seal reduces leakage, while a readable label helps correct use. Packaging adds cost and waste, so the design should fit the product and customer need. Saying product or promotion does not explain what the container actually does.

blocks.heading: Putting the idea to work
blocks.text: Nela Soup uses a secure food container and a clear label showing contents and handling information. Containment reduces spills during the journey; information helps customers use and identify the meal. A colourful logo can help recognition but does not by itself explain protection.

blocks.heading: Keeping the ideas apart
blocks.text:
Explain why “promotion” alone does not identify the function of Nela Soup’s sealed container.

A function describes what the packaging does. Its seal contains the soup and reduces spills; its label can communicate contents or handling. Attracting attention can also be a packaging function, but it must be explained, for example an eye-catching design that helps the product stand out on a shelf. Writing only “promotion” names a marketing-mix element without stating what this container does.
